items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: the Professor, Higgins, says you can always identify an Englishman the minute he opens his mouth

ctx.x: He said you were talking what?

Posh. Well you know in Britain it’s like in the line of “My Fair Lady” they were singing and the Professor, Higgins, says you can always identify an Englishman the minute he opens his mouth, you can immediately identify him. It’s like, and it still is to a certain extent, a class distinction there. You know if you go to a proper school, I would say old chap. It would be actual boy and jolly good show, you know this kind of an accent, a southern or sophisticated accent, which comes probably with the schools and…
whatever, has this accent. And it immediately identifies him, that he went to a good college, and so consequently in comes this little bit of prejudice you know.
